title: Unanswered
description: Ruling 7's one shape for every refusal, absence or 'not carried' across the placement seams: why (the seam's own typed reason), when to come back, and what can be done meanwhile, plus an escalation on a repeat ask. The base envelope leaves `why` unconstrained on purpose, as objects/answer leaves `value`: a per-seam envelope narrows it with `allOf` to that seam's reason (objects/item-absence `$defs.UnansweredItemAbsence`, views/placement-explanation-view's refusals), so the wire stays monomorphic and no TypeScript generic is needed (CONVENTIONS rule 11). Serialization: `comeBack` is internally tagged by `when`, `meanwhile` by `local`, kebab-case tags and camelCase fields; `escalation` is always written and is null when this is not a repeat ask (one provenance: null means 'not a repeat', never 'unknown'). Wire shape: this schema is the source of record; Rust mirror seam_contracts::Unanswered<R> / ComeBack / Meanwhile / Escalation (crates/seam-contracts/src/unanswered.rs). That module calls its `serde` derives (feature `serde`) the internal convenience form, yet they carry the same tags and field names, and a seam adapter that writes this envelope from them must serialize to this schema; no test pins the two yet (follow-on: a seam-contracts contract test that serializes every ComeBack, Meanwhile and Escalation form and validates it here). Source of truth: the seam that answered, per request (Category C): a wire envelope for an answer, never persisted as an entity of its own.

why.description: The seam's own typed reason. Unconstrained in the base envelope; a per-seam envelope narrows it.

comeBack.title: ComeBack
comeBack.description: When the answer can change: a time a tier or gate gave (`at`), or an event after which it can change (`on-event`, e.g. tier-reachable, posture-changed, parameters-declared, berth-offered). The core never reads it from a local clock: the time is supplied by whoever gave it.

epochSecs.description: The time to come back, in seconds since the Unix epoch. A u64 in Rust, bounded here to 9007199254740991 (2^53 - 1, the largest integer every JSON reader, JavaScript included, holds exactly); a larger value is refused, never rounded.

meanwhile.title: Meanwhile
meanwhile.description: What the asker can do locally while the request is unanswered. `nothing` must say why, so 'nothing' is a statement and never a gap.

oneOf.title: MeanwhileRunHere
oneOf.description: The device can do it itself.

oneOf.title: MeanwhileBuiltInInForce
oneOf.description: A built-in default is answering in its place.

because.description: Why nothing can be done locally.

oneOf.title: Escalation
oneOf.description: Set on a repeat ask before come-back: the answer escalates rather than repeats.

asked.description: How many times the request has been asked, this ask included, so the first escalation is 2 (`Unanswered::escalate`).

changed.description: What changed since the last answer, said even when it is "nothing".

escalation.description: Null unless this is a repeat ask before come-back.
